overview: Black prepares ...d5 with ...c6, a flexible reply that can become a Slav, a Caro-Kann-like set-up or a reversed English set-up. White usually plays 2.d4, 2.g3 or 2.c4 and Black follows with ...d5, reaching Slav, Réti or Catalan-style structures. The root has few games of its own and the play depends on the transposition.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with d4 and e4 or go for a fianchetto and c4 pressure.
Keep the move order flexible and choose a set-up after ...d5.

black_ideas.idea: Play ...d5 and develop a Slav-style set-up with ...Bf5 or ...Nf6 and ...e6.
Keep a solid pawn on c6 and meet central play with ...d5.

typical_structures.structure: Slav or Caro-Kann-type structure with pawns on c6 and d5.

character.notes: Black's c6-d5 formation is solid and hard to break down.

structure.notes: Not yet fixed; the centre is undecided.

approach.notes: A flexible reply to 1.Nf3 that strong players use now and then.

character.reason: Black builds the solid c6-d5 Slav-type set-up.

approach.reason: Respectable, less common reply to 1.Nf3, not a system.
